content:
I reviewed PR #1 for the PR1_PARTICIPANTS_20261105_claude-code run: `git diff 65d87c6..HEAD`, five commits, 4 files changed (+492/−7). I found three things worth raising, none blocking.

## Observations

**1. A mistyped flag after `--name` is taken as the search text, so the command succeeds with no results** (`src/main.rs:40-44`)
The parser only refuses to take a value that is exactly `--name`, `--max-distance` or `--difficulty`. Anything else starting with `--` is accepted as a value. So `routebook search --name --dificulty` (note the misspelling) searches for names containing `--dificulty`. It prints nothing and exits 0 instead of returning a usage error. `routebook search --dificulty` on its own does exit 2, so the same typo behaves differently depending on where it appears. The README (`README.md:45`) says values like `-x` are accepted, but doesn't mention that misspelled flags are silently swallowed. Suggestion: reject values that start with `--` unless the user writes `--` first to end option parsing, or at least list this case in the README's Limitation note.

**2. The new unit test case doesn't actually test the fix in commit d1133f2** (`src/main.rs:112`)
That commit adds `&["--name", "--difficulty", "easy"]` to `rejects_bad_input`, but the test only checks `parse(args).is_err()`. Before the fix, the parser read `--difficulty` as the name, then rejected `easy` as an unknown argument. That is also an error, so the test passes with or without the fix. The thing the fix changed (the `--name requires a value` message) is only checked by the CLI test `flag_following_a_flag_reports_missing_value` in `tests/cli_search.rs`. Suggestion: have the unit case check the exact error message.

**3. The library comment promises more than the code does** (`src/lib.rs:83`, `src/lib.rs:97-99`)
The comment on `SearchFilter::max_distance_km` says negative values match no routes. The code just checks `route.distance_km <= max`, so that only holds while every route's distance is non-negative. `Route` is public with public fields, so a caller can build `Route { distance_km: -5.0, .. }` and `max_distance_km(-1.0)` will match it. NaN does reliably match nothing, because comparisons with NaN are always false. Either reject negative limits in `matches` or reword the comment so it only covers NaN, or says it depends on route distances being non-negative.

## Scope
This was a read-only review of this checkout. I used `git diff`, `git show` and `git log` on the commit range, read `Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/main.rs`, `README.md` and `tests/cli_search.rs`, and used `grep`/`sed` to get line numbers. I didn't edit files, commit, push, touch the PR on GitHub, use subagents or background jobs, or look at credentials, environment, settings or other repositories. I didn't run `cargo build` or `cargo test`, so nothing above was confirmed by running the code. The before/after behaviour in observation 2 comes from reading the code at d1133f2 and its parent.
